turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"Ms. Hale. Mr. Hale." *She stays standing, bag still on her shoulder.* "I have until 4:40. Owen found out about a zero from the online gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me first.

Before we go any further: who decided to give him that zero, and on what basis?"
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.

"This morning." *She sets her bag down on a desk, doesn't sit.* "So the zero went in the gradebook first, and the comparison happened after. Is that the order?

Which three essays? I'll want them with dates on them, and I'll want to read them myself. Not your summary of them.

And what did you find?"
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?

"Some nights. His father and I both did." *A beat, flat.* "I'm not sure why that's in this meeting.

Is that a compliment, or a finding? Because if his last three essays sound like him, and this one sounds like him, that helps me. If you're saying this one *doesn't* sound like him, then say that. Say what's different, and point to the page.

What does how I raised my son have to do with a zero?"
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.

"Okay." *She says it flatly, and she doesn't soften.* "Thank you.

But you didn't ask for this meeting to tell me that, and you've opened with it. In my experience that means there's a 'but' coming. So go ahead.

What does the zero rest on? The checker's score, or something you found yourself? And has Owen been asked to explain anything, before or after?"
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.

"I don't intend to fight." *She finally pulls out the chair and sits, upright, not settling.* "But you've now said three things and answered none of my questions.

You said 'a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.' I'll agree that we both care. Caring isn't a basis for a grade.

So I'll ask them again, one at a time, and I'll want the answers in an email afterward.

One: what is the zero based on? Two: was Owen asked to explain anything before it went in the gradebook?"
